items.text: Housing statutes in many jurisdictions bar refusal to rent on race, religion, or national origin.
Employment law commonly forbids hiring or firing based on sex, race, or religion.
Public-accommodation rules require hotels and restaurants to serve people without regard to race.
Voting-rights statutes make it unlawful to put extra tests in the way of a qualified voter because of race.
Disability accommodations at work are a statutory duty in several systems, not a favour.
Schools that take public funds are often barred from excluding a student for race or national origin.
Credit statutes can forbid denying a loan because of sex or marital status.
Equal-pay rules compare wages for substantially equal work across sex.
A workplace may not generally use religion as the reason to skip a promotion.
Fair-housing posters in many cities list the protected classes for rental ads.
Jury service cannot usually be stripped for race. That is a civic-rights rule, not a courtesy.
Immigration status is separated from race in several anti-discrimination codes, and both have their own clauses.
A union hall that takes referrals may be under the same hiring bar as the employer.
Public employers typically cannot demote someone for filing a discrimination complaint.
Language-access rules in some courts require an interpreter so a party is not shut out.
Age-discrimination statutes in employment often start at a stated age and cover hiring and layoff.
Family-status protections in housing can stop a landlord from refusing a household with children.
A transit agency that takes public money may have to keep stops accessible.
Retaliation for reporting discrimination is itself a separate violation in many codes.
Professional licensing boards are often barred from using race as a gate on the exam.
Military equal-opportunity regulations cover harassment complaints inside the service.
A city human-rights office can take a public-accommodation complaint and issue findings.
Title of a housing ad that names a racial preference is the kind of text those statutes reach.
Pregnancy is treated as a sex-discrimination issue in several employment codes, with leave rules attached.
